Clear the enemies and reach the boss!
Welcome back to reality, traveler. Or rather, what's left of it. I am Sarah, commander of the Meridian's Wardens. Breathe — we caught you mid-transfer. Your body is still deciding when it is.
...Where am I? Princeton? Orléans? The sky... it tore apart, and something pulled.

An extraction beam. The ones who fired it call themselves the Unbound — a sect from my century that went to war over the right to touch the past, and lost. Losing made them desperate. Now they attack history itself: cracking open its pivotal moments and draining them, remaking time in their favor. You were a target. You are the one we reached in time.
Then we must stop them. But what of the soldiers I saw? They looked like my people, but... wrong. Their eyes glowed, their weapons hummed with light.

The Unbound's doing. Where their siphons deploy, they neural-link the local inhabitants and force them to defend the machines as 'Altered Mobs' — steam automatons overcharged with chronal energy, knights with energy shields. Alongside them you will face the Unbound's own infantry from the future. Destroy the siphons, and the link breaks.

Time protects itself. When they tore your moment open, history armed the only anchor it had left — you. Everything your era is poured itself into its legend rather than let them take it. We call it Temporal Resonance.
Your combat resonance is calibrated. Now let's test your spatial awareness — you'll need every advantage to navigate the fractured timelines.
Calibration complete. The time portals are unlocked — return to the bridge and choose your first destination.
Florence... it's beautiful, but I hear the hum of machinery. These scaffoldings aren't from my books.

Stay alert. The Unbound have deployed a siphon in Da Vinci's workshop. The city guards have been neural-linked. They are armed with shock-pikes. Do not let their electrical discharges lock your movements.
You dare interrupt the harvest? The Unbound have promised Florence eternity — and promised me your resonance.
Eternity built on stolen memories is no gift. Stand aside, or fall with your siphon.
The siphon is shattered. The energy is dispersing.
Outstanding. With the siphon gone, the neural-link is broken. The altered guards will wake with nothing but a headache, thinking it was a strange dream.
And the master of this workshop? Half-built wonders, ink still warm on the drafting table... and no Da Vinci. Where is he?
...I don't know. The record says he never left this room in 1503. Yet the era stands — as if history is holding its breath for him. Come home. I need to look at the other eras.

The bridge is yours, traveler. This ship is cut off from my own century, so what you see is what we have — the Chronal Repository will bank your dust, and the Holodeck can spar you against simulated foes.
When you are ready, the Temporal Portal is charged for your next destination. History is waiting.

TEMPORAL PORTAL DORMANT — the timeline is restored.
To everyone who held the timeline together.
LEVEL 2: THE SIEGE OF ORLÉANS — ORLÉANS 1429
Break through the English lines toward the siege works.
The barriers are down. Take the battlement.
Orléans is starving behind those walls. And that shimmer across the causeway — no siege line in 1429 glows like that.

That is Unbound hardware. Kinetic shield generators pinning the French vanguard in place, and mortar emplacements ranged on every approach. Break the generators and the cavalry charge history remembers can finally happen.
So the little ghost walks through my barriers. The Unbound bought me this siege, traveler, and I intend to keep it until the walls come down.
You sold a city for borrowed lightning. Put down the lance and I might leave you your century.
The last generator is slag. The barriers are gone.
Confirmed. The vanguard is moving. The relief of Orléans is back on its own timeline, and the English commanders will remember nothing but bad weather and worse luck.
The banner is still standing in the mud where they planted it, Commander. Nobody picked it up. Where is the Maid of Orléans?
Not on the field. Not in the camp. Not anywhere in 1429 that I can read. That is two eras now, both waiting on someone who never arrived.
Then log it and take me back to the ship. I want to know what they are waiting for.
Cross the fairgrounds and reach the Electricity Building
Rotate the conductive coils to route the beam into the receiver
The Court of Honor is open — press on!
Electric light for a mile in every direction — and every wire of it humming wrong.

That is Unbound work, Traveler. They have seeded siphon coils across the fairgrounds. Let the overload land and the Exposition burns with Tesla's name on it. Reroute the current before the crowds pay for it.
Do you feel it? Alternating. Accelerating. A century of progress, and I can spend all of it in one beautiful second.
Then spend it on me. Leave the fair out of it.
Siphon coils are shattered. The current is running where it should.
Readings are settling. Every lamp on the fairgrounds is still lit — and the crowd never knew.
The engineers were reading his notes aloud to each other, Sarah. Guessing. Tesla's own switch, and no Tesla.
Three. Florence, Orléans, Chicago. Every one of them missing the one person the moment was built around. I am starting to think that is the pattern, not the coincidence.
Then find me the pattern, Commander. Bring me home.
Breach the Bastille and reach the inner courtyard
Caught in the beam! The dampener is draining your Ultimate — break the light
Blow the cell locks and free the prisoners ({0}/{1})
The prisoners have hauled the gate open — breach the inner courtyard
INNER COURTYARD BARRED — FREE THE PRISONERS
The Bastille. The crowd is at the gates — and something inside is answering them with searchlights.
Those are neural-dampening projectors, not lamps. Stay out of the beams: every second in the light bleeds off your Ultimate Meter. The Unbound want this uprising too tired to finish what it started.
Citizen! You are charged with sedition against the Unbound. The verdict is recorded, the sentence is eternal — and the mob will carry it out for me.
You did not come here to free anyone. You came to keep them shouting so nobody notices the siphon. Court adjourned.
The siphon is shattered. The projectors are dark.
Confirmed. The dampening field is collapsing and the prisoners are already through the inner gate. Paris takes the Bastille tonight — on its own terms, the way it was written.
They took the gate themselves in the end. I only cleared the way.
That is the job, and it is going to keep being the job. Come home — I have four more eras on the board and a question I do not like the shape of.
Ask it out loud next time, Commander. Bring me home.
Climb sternward before the flooding overtakes you
Reach the boat deck — the water is still rising
The harvest is broken. Return to the Time-Ship.
The deck is already tilting. This ship has hours. Maybe less.

The Unbound are not siphoning a battle this time, Traveler. They are draining grief — fifteen hundred lives' worth, harvested at the exact moment history remembers it happening. Get sternward before the bow goes under.
Then we take their siphon before the sea takes the ship.
Traveler, the flooding is running ahead of the historical record. Something down there is pulling water in faster than the hull can take it.
It is not the sea doing this. It is them.
Their harvester is anchored at the stern rail. Engage it and that deck will not stay dry. Keep to the gantries and finish it fast.
Sixteen hundred endings, all in one hour. Do you understand how rare a yield like this is? Stand still. You are spoiling it.
This is not a harvest. It is a grave. And you are standing in it.
The siphon is down. The water is still rising.
It has to. The sinking is real history and history stands. What we stopped was the theft — those people will be remembered instead of drained. The lifeboats are launching on schedule now.
There is something left in the wreck of the harvester. Encrypted. It keeps repeating one string.

Route it to me. Traveler, that is an uplink handshake. The Unbound were never storing this haul aboard — it was relaying it upward, to an orbital communications relay that will not exist for another fifty-seven years.
Then that is where the rest of the timeline is going. Get me back to the ship, Sarah. We follow it up.
Cross the death strip unseen and reach the radar yard
In the light! A drone strike lands in seconds — break line of sight
Cut the surveillance feed relays to darken the searchlights ({0}/{1})
Every beam is dark and the radar gate is open — reach the bunker street
RADAR GATE SEALED — CUT THE SURVEILLANCE FEEDS
They are still pouring the Wall and there are already searchlights on it. Those towers are not 1961.

They are cloaked radar masts, Traveler, and the beams under them are targeting paint. Stand in one longer than a second and a half and something above the cloud deck fires straight down the column. Keep to the dark, and cut the feed relays where you find them — a mast with no feed is a mast with no beam.
Far enough. Behind me is a switchboard that speaks to every silo on this continent, and tonight it tells them a lie they have been waiting fifteen years to believe. You will not reach it.
You cut a wall through the middle of a living city and called it order. I am going to come through you the same way they will come through it.
The switchboard is dead. The masts are dark all the way to the horizon.
Confirmed. The launch order never went out. Berlin gets to survive its own division the hard, slow, human way — which is the way it was written.
Sarah, I went up that mast faster than I could have in Florence. It is getting easier, not harder.
Because it is growing. Every scrap you take back off their machines stays in you — that is the one account they cannot drain. Keep it. The eras ahead are heavier than this one.
Then let it grow, and get me to the next one. Bring me home, Commander.
Wade the shifting dunes and find a way beneath the siege line
Find the hieroglyph seal — the order is carved somewhere in the tombs
Press the glyphs in the carved order ({0}/{1})
The vault is open — reach Cleopatra's chambers before the legion does
HIEROGLYPH SEAL — PRESS THE GLYPHS IN THE CARVED ORDER
CARVED ORDER — SCARAB · IBIS · FALCON · JACKAL
Roman siege towers on the shore — and every legionnaire down there is carrying a blade that burns.

Plasma swords and powered centurion plate, Traveler. The Unbound are buying Octavian a total victory and siphoning the fall of Alexandria while it burns. The palace guard is on the same neural link. Get under the sand line: the tomb network runs beneath the siege and comes up inside the royal vault.
Then I go through the dead to reach the living.
The queen's vault opens only for those who know the old order, little ghost. I wrote the order. I wrote her ending. Kneel and be catalogued.
You put a leash on her own guard and called it worship. Step away from the door.
The Jackal Priest is beaten, and the guards breathe freely again... but these are the queen's own chambers. Where is Cleopatra?

Nowhere. Her guards defended an empty throne with future fire. And the era holds its breath — like Florence. Like Orléans. That makes every one of them now. Every giant, missing from their own moment.
Torn loose, as I was? Adrift somewhere between the timelines?
That is my hope. We caught you mid-theft — perhaps the others tore free and are drifting where we can search. The Observation Deck is already scanning the shards. We will find them.
The siphon is shattered. The sand is just sand again.
Confirmed. The neural link is down across the whole delta. Octavian's legion and the palace guard both come back to themselves, and the siege ends the way history wrote it — not one hour worse.
The vault is sealed and the delta is quiet. It is the emptiest victory I have carried out of an era yet.
Act II runs harder than Act I, Traveler, and every anchor ahead is bigger than one palace. Whatever you reclaimed in there is yours now — you are going to need all of it.
Then stop warning me and take me home, Commander. There is another one waiting.
Get the citizens out before Vesuvius buries the city
Balance the winch — both stone pans must carry the same load
The road east is open. Run.
The flow caught you — keep moving east!
Reach the thermal anchor on the caldera rim
The harvest is broken. Return to the Time-Ship.
ROAD BURIED — HAUL THE ROCKFALL CLEAR
The mountain is already open. That ash column is miles high — and it is coming down far faster than it should be.

Faster is the whole point, Traveler. The Unbound have driven thermal anchors into the caldera to tap the eruption at its peak. They are forcing Vesuvius ahead of its own schedule so the yield lands before anyone in Pompeii can reach the harbour.
Then I get them to the harbour first. The anchor second.
Eighteen hours of terror, compressed into two. Do you understand what that concentration is worth? Every one of them running, and not one of them fast enough.
They were never running from the mountain. They were running from you.
The anchor is down. The mountain sounds ordinary again — as ordinary as that ever gets.
Confirmed. Vesuvius is back on its own clock: eighteen hours, exactly the way it was written. That is enough time. The south road is moving and the harbour is answering.
Every road out of that city was somebody's last idea, Sarah. Not one of them belonged to a great name. It was just people, and they still got out.

They did — and you came out of it carrying more than you walked in with. Everything you take back off their machines stays in you. Meanwhile Okafor has the shard search running again. Mozart should have been at a keyboard in 1787, and there is nobody at it.
Log it, and bring me home. There are nine more of these.
The Navy is shelling the harbour. Get to the moorings.
Cross the channel and board the burning flagship.
The targeting grid is dead. Return to the Time-Ship.
They voted. A whole town of thieves stood up and voted itself free — and the sky is full of mortars.

Those are not Navy guns, Traveler, not entirely. The Unbound have seeded the water with sub-aquatic torpedoes and laid a chronal targeting grid over the bay. Every shell the British fire is being aimed for them. Nassau is not being defeated. It is being erased on schedule.
Then we go where the grid is anchored. Out to the ships.
Look at it burn. A republic of nobodies, and history was going to keep the name anyway. I am simply correcting the ledger.
They are not nobodies. They are the first people here who chose. Get off their harbour.
The grid is down. The guns are just guns again.
Confirmed — the bay is clear of chronal returns. Nassau still falls to the pardon in two years, Traveler, but it falls the way it actually fell, and everyone below decks gets to run for the boats.
They voted themselves free and then held the harbour with what they had. Nobody down there needed a legend to tell them how.
No. And every era that did have one is still missing them. Come home and let the ship read you — there is another siphon burning three hundred years further back, and I do not like where.
Cross the yard and get up onto the stage
Cross the stage — the boards shake before they drop
The galleries have you marked — move!
Swing the rigging up through the galleries to the tiring-house
Full house. Two thousand people packed in to watch a prince go mad, and not one of them has blinked since I walked in.

That is the manipulators, Traveler. The Unbound have seeded the galleries, and they have rigged collapse charges under the stage. The moment those boards go, two thousand held minds are released at once and they all try to leave through the same door. Keep off a plank that starts shaking — and keep moving. A held crowd throws whatever is in reach at anything that stands still.
Then I will give them a performance worth watching.
You are early, and you are not in the script. Sit down. The fifth act is the only part of any of this that anyone remembers, and I have rewritten it so that nobody walks out.
Every one of them came here to watch a tragedy and then go home again. I am going to make sure they do.
Charges are out from under the boards. The galleries let go all at once — listen to them. They are arguing about the ending.
Confirmed. Two thousand people walk out of the Globe tonight and take that argument home with them, which is exactly what was written.
They held the curtain on an unfinished fifth act, Sarah. The prompt-book just... stops. Nobody has seen the author in days.
Of course they haven't. Add him to the list. It is getting long enough that I have stopped calling it a coincidence on the log.
Then log it and line up the next one. Bring me home, Commander.
Advance east across the battlefield — use the fences and sandbags for cover.
Both arrays are down. The Union line has the breastwork — follow it into the railcut.
CONFEDERATE BREASTWORK — BREAK THE SHIELDING ARRAYS
That is not cannon fire. Those shells are tracking — they turn to follow me.

Confirmed. The Unbound handed the Confederate batteries laser guidance and an electromagnetic screen, and Union brigades are pinned in the open. Two shielding arrays hold that screen up. Break both and the line moves. Keep something solid between you and the sky, Traveler — those guns telegraph before they fire.
RAILHEAD SECURE. TARGET RESOLVED. THE FIELD BELONGS TO THE GUN.
Then come off the rails and say that where I can reach you.
The gun is dead. The sky is quiet. First time all day I can hear the wheat.

Siphon shattered — the whole Gettysburg draw just went dark on my board. The Union advance is over the wall and the battle is running on its own clock again. Whatever the Unbound wrote here is unwritten.
The dedication platform is built and empty, Sarah. The address unread. The officers have had no word from Washington in days.
Six now. Six of history's heaviest, and not one of them standing where the record says they stood. We find the pattern or we lose the next one.
Log it. Then pull me out. There are four more of these.
Cross the mare and reach the Unbound outpost
Mind the vacuum vents — the low route is the loud route
Ride the spire lift and take the highline over the curtain wall
The broadcast is clean. Return to the Time-Ship.
Tranquility Base is right there. The lander, the flag, the first footprints ever pressed into this dust — and half a kilometre east of it, something the crew will never see and never report.

That is the relay, Traveler. The uplink handshake we pulled out of the Titanic wreck was pointing here all along — fifty-seven years early, and this is the address. The Unbound are riding the broadcast: six hundred million people watching one moment together, and every one of them feeding the siphon. Watch your footing. One sixth of the gravity you are used to, and the outpost vents run straight to vacuum.
Then we take the relay before the broadcast ends.
To think humanity would walk among the stars... and yet, the Unbound have built a fortress of metal here.

Their last siphon nexus. Break it, and their roads through the rifts begin to close. And my trace is nearly done — every drained era, every stolen scrap of resonance... it has all been flowing somewhere. This siphon will show me where.
The nexus siphon buckles and goes dark. On the Time-Ship, Sarah's trace completes.

...Coordinates. A fortress in the space between timelines. And inside it — resonance signatures. Alive. It's them. {CaptiveName1}. {CaptiveName2}. The others we lost. They were never adrift. The Unbound have had them since the first strike — and their resonance is draining.
Then the eras were never the whole of it. Whatever they are building with the stolen years, it ends now. Set the portal, Commander.

Six hundred million witnesses, one signal, one instant. Do you know what a species remembers hardest? The first time it left. I will take that from them, and they will never learn the shape of the hole where it was.
They came up here on arithmetic and nerve, and they came up here together. You do not get to hold that.
The relay is scrap. The broadcast is going out clean.

Confirmed. Every set on Earth is watching the real thing. The outpost crew the Unbound pressed into service are already coming back to themselves — nobody down there will remember having been anything but themselves.
I have never felt it this strong, Sarah. Everything I pulled off their machines up here is still in my hands.
Hold on to it. The overload wrote a coordinate signature back down the beam before it died, and it is not anywhere in history — it is outside it. That is where they have been keeping them.
Then Act Two ends here. Take me through their front door, Commander.
Cross the rift and find the far corridor
Ride the loose era fragments — the shelf below is pooled with stalled time
The corridor is open. Return to the Time-Ship.

There is no ground here. There is no here here — only pieces. That is the flag from Tranquility Base, and that is a Bastille door, and they are falling past each other without either of them falling down.

You are between dimensions, Traveler. The trace we pulled off the Overseer runs straight through it — the Unbound cut a corridor from their own century back through every fracture they ever made, and this is the spoil heap. Head east. The far side opens on the fortress.
Then I walk east on Orléans stone and Titanic decking. Tell me the moment the gravity is about to turn over.
You are the one that got away. They modelled you a thousand times to find out how — and I am the model that kept getting up.
Then you know exactly how I fight. So do I. Come on.
It went down the way I would have gone down. Same guard, same tell, same half-second too late. I have never had to watch myself lose before.

The corridor is holding. There was no siphon in here to shatter — the rift stopped tearing the moment that thing stopped drawing on it. And nothing living was ever caught in the Void, so there is nobody down there to send home. For once I have no casualty list to read you.
It fought like me, Sarah. Every guard, every tell. Somebody has been studying me long enough to build that.

Long enough to build it a thousand times over, by the look of this corridor. They are not improvising, and they have not been improvising since the first strike. The far end of this is their front door, and it is standing open.
Then let it be me who walks through it. Take me to the Bastion, Commander.
Time the perimeter lattice and breach the outer rampart
Ride the containment pockets across the Extraction Hall
Run the Forge spine to the core
The intake is dead. The Forge is firing — ride the channel.
There is no sky here. No ground either — just the fortress, hanging in the space between one century and the next.

That is the Bastion, Traveler. Not a stolen era: the place they built outside all of them, and the room every siphon in history reported back to. It was made to keep people out, so the perimeter will be honest about it — security lattices on a fixed cycle, and anti-gravity containment fields they use to shift cargo. Read a lattice before you walk it. And mind the pockets: they will lift you a great deal further than you expect.
Then let us walk into the one place they never rehearsed losing.
You are a rounding error that learned to knock. I have catalogued every version of this conversation, and in the ones that matter you were filed a long time ago.
You have catalogued an awful lot of people who never got to answer you. I am the answer.
The intake is dark. Every siphon line in the Bastion went slack at once.

Confirmed — and the cradles are still holding. I want you to hear that part: we could not cut one of them loose, and the engine at the core is still charged. They come home when it dies, and not one minute before.
Then it dies today. The whole hall pulled at me on the way out, Sarah, and I am still carrying every scrap I took back off them.
Good, because there is exactly one route left and it is theirs. The Forge is firing, and the channel it opens only exists while it fires. We ride it in.
Then put me in the channel, Commander. One jump left, and nothing after it.
Ride the firing channel down to the Meridian Founding
Climb the founding terraces and force a way east
RUN — the channel is closing behind you
Clear the guard at the anchor seat
Seal the timeline at the half-seated Prime Anchor
The Prime Anchor is shattered. Every thread goes home.
Press Interact to seal the timeline
This is no era I can read. There is a city being founded down there, under a sky that has not decided what century it is.

The founding day of the Meridian, Traveler — everything my order ever was starts this morning. The Forge fired at it, and the channel you rode in on is the shot. The First Unbound is already at the seat with the Prime Anchor half in.
Then we finish it where they started it.
The seat is through that door. Everything you have taken back since Florence is riding in you right now, and it is the one weight their anchor was never built to out-hold.
Standing over the stone with three phases of Unbound doctrine and a war it refuses to have lost. This is the last door, Traveler. There is nothing after this one.

You are a footnote that learned to walk. I have unwritten empires, languages, entire centuries of a species that never noticed the subtraction. This morning I unwrite the order that beat me — and then I come back for the line in the ledger with your name on it.
You have been paying for me with other people's centuries since the first day. I am here to close the account.
It is down — and the Anchor is exposed, half in and still holding. That is it, Traveler. Walk to the stone and seal it. Everything you have carried since the workshop goes into that one press.
Every era. All the way back.
It's shattering! The Forge is drinking its own backlash — the cradles are opening! The resonance — all of it — it's going home!

Threads of light arc out of the collapsing Prime Anchor and across every era. In Renaissance Florence, in Roman Pompeii, on the fields of Gettysburg, cybernetic gear, laser visors and glowing energy cells dissolve from guards, soldiers and citizens. In the Bastion the cradles open one after another, and the legends — and the hundreds behind them — dissolve into golden light and reappear each in their own moment.
The resonance... it was never mine. It was history's — held in trust. Take it back.

The timelines are sealed. The war is over — and the future you saved is the one you're standing in. Thank you, traveler. You will wake where they tried to take you from. You will remember the Time-Ship, the battle, and the friends you fought beside... but the rifts are closed forever. You are going home.
History... is ours to write now.
The traveler disappears — last of all the legends. The Founding's sky clears, and the Meridian's first day proceeds, untouched.

en: and the nexus question is per-hero.

We couldn't stop the beam. We could hold it — a few seconds. That was enough for the fire to finish catching. You are the one they fired on and did not get. Now — we calibrate it. Step up to the bay console.
...Where am I? My study. Princeton — the blackboard was an arm's length away. The sky tore apart over the elms, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The vanguard field before Orléans. I had the banner in my hands. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? My workshop. Florence — the ornithopter was still on the bench. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The field at Gettysburg. I had not finished the address. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? My own chambers. Alexandria — the envoys were still waiting. The sky tore apart above the palace, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The laboratory. The coil was still singing. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The Globe. The fifth act unwritten on the table. The sky tore apart above the yard, and something pulled.
...Where am I? Vienna — mid-concerto, the hall holding its breath. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The Tidewater. The river path home. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.

en: My own workshop, held open by their machine while I stood in it. They will have to find another way to stop me finishing the work.

They had. Florence is still waiting for its master, though. Two eras, and only one of them got its legend back.
Every lamp on the fairground is lit and the switch is under my own hand again. They came for the man, Sarah, not the machine.
Then Florence and Orléans are the same crime under a different name. Two eras still waiting on someone who never arrived. Come home.
The Jackal Priest is beaten, and my guards breathe freely again. They held these chambers against a throne they had been told was empty.
They did — and every other era on my board is still holding its breath. Florence. Orléans. Every giant, missing from their own moment. You are the only one of them standing in theirs.
The fifth act is finished and the house went home arguing about it. They only ever needed the author in the room.
Then you are the lucky one. Every other era on the log is still waiting on someone who never walked in. Bring me that list at the ship.
The platform is standing and the address is in my coat, Sarah. They meant for it never to be read.
Five others were not so fortunate. Five of history's heaviest, and not one of them standing where the record says they stood. We find the pattern or we lose the next one.

en: By every saint and star... the hall goes on beyond sight. The legends — wired into the machines like lamps into a chandelier. And behind them... hundreds more.

Extraction Cradles. This is where every stolen era went — they were never spending the energy, they were banking it. All of it feeds that engine at the core. Do NOT touch the cradles! Sever a thread while the machine is charged and the machine keeps them — forever. The only way to free them is to kill it.

The Warden is half right. It is called the Anchor Forge, little legend, and it was calibrated for all of you. The others we caged before their fire could catch. Yours caught — history flinched, and hid itself inside you. Every era we burned since, we burned to fill the hole you left. The deficit in my ledger carries your name. Lie down in a cradle — and history keeps the rest.
My legacy is not yours to spend. I will break your Forge — and every thread in this hall goes home.

en: Four eras closed and four legends unaccounted for, traveler. I am not calling that a coincidence on the log any more.
Whatever you took back off their machines out there stays with you. Carry it to the next one — Act Two runs harder.
Every era you seal cuts one more of their roads, and you come back off each one heavier than you went in. That is the only arithmetic in this war that runs our way.
The Observation Deck is still sweeping the shards for the others. Nothing yet. The portal is charged when you are.
No more eras, traveler. From here it is their ground, their corridor and their fortress, and there is no way back to this deck between them.
Everything history handed you is still in your hands. Take all of it through that portal.
Medic Okafor. Sit, please — I read every traveler before and after. Your resonance baseline is up eleven points since Florence.
That is not what the Commander expected, and I would rather she were wrong in this direction. Go carefully.
Up again. Whatever you are pulling out of their siphons is not passing through you, traveler — it is staying.
I have also finished the era sweep the Commander asked for. Vienna, 1787. No Mozart. I have stopped being surprised and started keeping a list.
The readings are off my scale now. I have nothing to compare you to except the day we pulled you off that beam.
Come back and let me take one more. That is all I am asking of you.
